verdicts.quote: “We’ve defined a set of scopes based on the OAuth 2.1 standard… Both the Admin and Shopper APIs are authorized using an access token in the form of a JSON Web Token (JWT)… included… as an HTTP header that follows the Bearer authentication scheme… Shopper API token | Create a SLAS client… Admin API token | Create an API client in Account Manager.”
verdicts.reason: Docs explicitly describe OAuth 2.x-based flows (SLAS and Account Manager) with Bearer JWTs.

verdicts.quote: “For B2C Commerce customers, the API is available at no extra cost.”
verdicts.reason: Access is limited to paying customers (and their admins provision clients), not self‑serve credentials; this implies engaging Salesforce to become a customer.

verdicts.quote: “sfcc.analytics … Analytics …; sfcc.catalogs … Read catalog information…; sfcc.catalogs.rw … Create, read, update, and delete catalogs.”
verdicts.reason: The scopes catalog shows many Admin families with read/write CRUD plus numerous Shopper families in the references, indicating broad surface.

verdicts.quote: “B2C MCP: Connect your assistant to B2C Commerce tools, official documentation search… and general‑purpose SCAPI Admin API access… For clients that require manual MCP configuration, use npx … @salesforce/b2c-dx-mcp.”
verdicts.reason: The MCP is documented by Salesforce and distributed under the @salesforce namespace, indicating an official server.

verdicts.quote: “To access an on-demand sandbox, you must purchase sandbox credits, enable appropriate permissions and users, and configure a client API ID.”
verdicts.reason: There’s no self‑serve dev org/credentials; customers’ admins must create API clients in Account Manager, so building and testing requires a customer org or partner access (sales/partnership first).
